title: shield-should-be-language
goal: Shield should be language-agnostic — support Gradle/Java projects. Currently src/skills/shield/handler.ts is tightly coupled to TypeScript: stepCommand() reads package.json, driftCheck() parses TS exports, securityScan() looks for TS-specific patterns (process.env, child_process), yagniCheck() counts LOC/imports in .ts files. For Java/Gradle projects shield either fails (no package.json → stepCommand = null → SKIP) or misses real issues. Solution: refactor shield into ShieldAdapter interface (src/core/shield/adapter.ts), move current TS logic into TypeScriptAdapter, implement GradleAdapter (checkstyle/PMD for lint, javac for type-check, ./gradlew test for tests, AST scanner for drift, Java security patterns). Config via orionShield.json, auto-detect language by markers (build.gradle → Gradle/Java, package.json → TS/Node.js, pom.xml → Maven/Java). Keep all existing TS tests passing unchanged.
constraints: Don't break existing TS projects, all current tests (916) must pass unchanged, no new runtime dependencies (Gradle/Java tools called via spawnSync). Auto-detect optional — no markers = TS fallback.
